svg.title: Who steers the WSL2 clock, and what happened when one hand let go
svg.desc: Top row, three situations. Ubuntu 24.04 default (documented): Windows/Hyper-V implicit sync and systemd-timesyncd can both write the Linux kernel clock; the project observed four REALTIME steps of +0.59 to +0.63 s while the service was active (C1 A0). Ubuntu 24.04 after systemctl stop (measured, D4R2): timesyncd is stopped but the unit is still enabled, Hyper-V remains, and the kernel tick was 10833 in the PRE snapshot about 60 s after the stop and 10000 in the later POST snapshot; who set or reset it is not established. Ubuntu 26.04 fresh default (documented): chrony runs with -x and reads only, so Hyper-V is the single default writer; a 300 s guest-side screen measured MONOTONIC against MONOTONIC_RAW at -0.50 to -0.46 ppm over the full run with all ten windows inside the plus or minus 1000 ppm screen. Bottom, the D4R2 replay: after the stop and an approximately 60 s hold, window 1 (0 to 30 s) measured +26,665.299 to +26,724.999 ppm against Windows QPC, outside the screen, about +0.80 s gained; windows 2 to 4 were within about plus or minus 33 ppm; the 120 s average was +6,661.607 to +6,676.217 ppm, still outside; RAW against QPC over 120 s was -6.323 to +8.190 ppm. Motion is playback only at ten times real time; with animation off the complete result is shown.
svg.text: Who steers the WSL2 clock, and what happened when one hand let go
Ubuntu 24.04 · WSL2 · historical experiment D4R2 · the chart replays published measurements at 10× real time
alternative default · different machine and reference
WHAT THE CLOCK DID AFTER THE STOP
CLOCK_MONOTONIC rate vs Windows QPC · measured, host-referenced · D4R2

g.text: Service active: two default writers can steer the same kernel clock.
systemctl stop confirmed; the unit stays enabled. The experiment now waits ≈60 s, timed by Windows QPC.
PRE snapshot: tick 10833, freq 2157314. The kernel is still set to correct. Window 1 is sampling…
Window 1: +26,665 to +26,725 ppm, about 2.7 % fast; ≈ +0.80 s gained (derived). Far outside the screen.
Windows 2–4: within ±33 ppm. The rate looks normal now, but the early lead is already banked.
120 s average: +6,662 to +6,676 ppm, still outside. One bad window dominates the mean.
Result: one bad window dominates the 120 s mean; RAW/QPC stayed near 0 → discipline, not hardware (inference).
−6.3 to +8.2 ppm · inside the screen · hardware counter near nominal
stopped write path · unit still enabled
cursor and sampling wash: illustrative, hidden when animation is off
Not established: who set tick 10833, what reset it, or that timesyncd was the sole writer (C1 remained INCONCLUSIVE).
26.04 card: different machine, guest-side reference — a bounded screen, not a qualification or a 24.04-vs-26.04 ranking.
